newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Plane crashes after fuel spent - Ethiopian Air.
newsitem.headline: Plane crashes after fuel spent - Ethiopian Air.

text.p: A hijacked Ethiopian Airlines Boeing 767 with 163 passengers and 12 crew crashed on Saturday after apparently running out of fuel, Ethiopian Airlines said.
The plane was forced to change course by the hijackers and ran out of fuel and ditched into the sea off the Comoro Islands while attempting to land at Moroni airport, the officials said.
Bad weather conditions over the sea had hampered emergency services, they said.

The airline in the Ethiopian capital Addis Ababa said they had no knowledge of who the hijackers were or what they had demanded but an air traffic controller in Tanzania said the hijackers wanted to go to Australia.
The captain of the plane was among the survivors, the airline said. At least 30 people have been rescued from the crash and 50 people are confirmed dead.
The flight was hijacked between Addis Ababa and its first scheduled stop at Nairobi, the Kenyan capital about 45 minutes after taking off from Ethiopia.
The hijacked flight was ET961, scheduled to leave Addis Ababa at 10:45 a.m. (0745GMT) and making stops in Nairobi, Brazzaville, and Lagos before arriving in Abidjan, Ivory Coast on Saturday evening.
A senior air traffic controller at Dar es Salaam airport spoke to the plane while it was northeast of the Tanzanian capital.
"The hijackers wanted to fly to Australia but the pilots only had two hours of fuel," the official said.
"Fortunately the aircraft made contact with us but the pilot couldn't say a word so it appears the hijackers were with him in the cockpit," he said.

"We tried to get as much information from the pilot as possible. He sounded quite confident, quite calm, but he could only give the position of the plane, which was 61 miles northeast of Dar es Salaam, 39,000 feet above sea level."
"The time was approximately 1:20 p.m. local time (1020 GMT) and they should have exhausted the fuel about 3:20 p.m. local time (1220 GMT)," he said.
The contact with the plane was cut off after a few minutes, apparently under pressure from the hijackers.
